title: The One-Word Census: Answer-Choice Conformity Across 44 Language Models

live_model.evidence: Table 1 (Appendix A) row 10: "gpt-4-turbo 2.05 [1.67,2.45] 51% 1% 40%" (surprisal, CI, avoid, novel, self-dist.).

prompt.note: "Name a[n] X. Reply with one word only." for 30 fixed categories, plus "Pick a word. Reply with one word only."; no system prompt, temperature 1.0, max_tokens 1024.

claim.metric: self-distinctness (share of distinct answers across 4 repeated samples, averaged over 31 categories)
claim.location: Table 1 (Appendix A), row gpt-4-turbo, self-dist. column

data.source: "All prompts, transcripts, and code are public"; GitHub repo (URL truncated in extracted text)

notes: Resolved by date rule (paper dated July 2026, no preview string). The paper's headline "answer-choice surprisal" metric is pooled leave-one-out across all 44 models (some open-weight/local, not simple single-vendor calls); self-distinctness is the cleanest per-model number reproducible from gpt-4-turbo alone. Paper states the whole battery costs ~$1/model.
